title.en: Volume 19: Shen Jiong; Yu Li; Ma Shu

sentences.zh: 陳書卷十九

translations.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 19
translations.idiomatic: Book of Chen, Volume 19

sentences.zh: 列傳第十三

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Thirteen
translations.idiomatic: Biographies, Part Thirteen

sentences.zh: 沈炯 虞荔 弟寄 馬樞

translations.literal: Shen Jiong; Yu Li; younger brother Ji; Ma Shu
translations.idiomatic: Shen Jiong; Yu Li; younger brother Ji; Ma Shu

sentences.zh: 沈炯字禮明，[1]吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Jiong, styled Liming, Editorial footnote marker 1. was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Jiong, styled Liming, [1] came from Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 祖瑀，梁尋陽太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yu was Administrator of Xunyang under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu had been Liang's administrator of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 父續，王府記室參軍。

translations.literal: His father Xu was a staff recorder in a princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xu was a recorder on a prince's staff.

sentences.zh: 炯少有雋才，為當時所重。

translations.literal: Jiong in youth had outstanding talent and was esteemed by his age.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong showed rare talent in youth and was held in esteem.

sentences.zh: 釋褐王國常侍，遷為尚書左民侍郎，出為吳令。

translations.literal: He doffed the commoner's garb as a kingdom regular attendant, was transferred to be Vice Minister of the Left for the People in the Secretariat, and went out as magistrate of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a kingdom regular attendant, rose to vice minister of the left for the people, and was posted as magistrate of Wu.

sentences.zh: 侯景之難，吳郡太守袁君正入援京師，以炯監郡。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion the Administrator of Wu commandery Yuan Junzheng entered to relieve the capital and made Jiong overseer of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion Yuan Junzheng, administrator of Wu, marched to relieve the capital and left Jiong to oversee the commandery.

sentences.zh: 京城陷，景將宋子仙據吳興，遣使召炯，委以書記之任。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, Jing's general Song Zixian held Wuxing and sent an envoy to summon Jiong, entrusting him with secretarial duties.
translations.idiomatic: The capital fell. Jing's general Song Zixian held Wuxing and summoned Jiong to keep his records.

sentences.zh: 炯固辭以疾，子仙怒，命斬之。

translations.literal: Jiong firmly declined on grounds of illness; Zixian was enraged and ordered him beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong pleaded illness and refused. Zixian flew into a rage and ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 炯解衣將就戮，礙於路間桑樹，乃更牽往他所，或遽救之，僅而獲免。

translations.literal: Jiong removed his robe to await the blade; he was hindered by a mulberry tree in the road, was then dragged elsewhere, and someone hastily rescued him—he barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped for the blade, but a mulberry in the road blocked the stroke. They dragged him elsewhere; someone rushed to save him, and he barely lived.

sentences.zh: 子仙愛其才，終逼之令掌書記。

translations.literal: Zixian loved his talent and in the end forced him to take charge of secretarial work.
translations.idiomatic: Zixian prized his gift for words and at last compelled him to keep the records.

sentences.zh: 及子仙為王僧辯所敗，僧辯素聞其名，於軍中購得之，酬所獲者鐵錢十萬，自是羽檄軍書皆出於炯。

translations.literal: When Zixian was defeated by Wang Sengbian, Sengbian had long heard his name and in the army ransomed him, rewarding the captor with one hundred thousand iron coins; from then on urgent dispatches and military documents all came from Jiong's hand.
translations.idiomatic: When Zixian fell to Wang Sengbian, Sengbian, who had long known his name, bought him out of the ranks for one hundred thousand iron coins. After that every dispatch and army paper bore Jiong's hand.

sentences.zh: 及簡文遇害，四方岳牧皆上表於江陵勸進，僧辯令炯製表，其文甚工，當時莫有逮者。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jianwen of Liang was killed, territorial governors everywhere sent memorials to Jiangling urging enthronement; Sengbian had Jiong draft the memorial—the writing was very skilled, and none of the time could match it.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Jianwen was killed, governors everywhere sent memorials to Jiangling urging a new throne. Sengbian had Jiong draft them. None of the age could match his craft.

sentences.zh: 高祖南下，與僧辯會于白茅灣，登壇設盟，炯為其文。

translations.literal: When the Founder marched south and met Sengbian at Baimao Bay, they ascended the altar and set the covenant; Jiong wrote its text.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder marched south he met Sengbian at Baimao Bay. They mounted the altar and swore alliance; Jiong wrote the words.

sentences.zh: 及侯景東奔至吳郡，獲炯妻虞氏，子行簡，並殺之，炯弟攜其母逃而獲免。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing fled east to Wu commandery he seized Jiong's wife, née Yu, and his son Xingjian, and killed them both; Jiong's younger brother carried off their mother and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing fled east into Wu commandery he seized Jiong's wife, Lady Yu, and his son Xingjian and killed them. Jiong's younger brother fled with their mother and lived.

sentences.zh: 侯景平，梁元帝愍其妻子嬰戮，特封原鄉縣侯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, Emperor Yuan of Liang pitied that his wife and children had died in the slaughter and specially enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yuanxiang with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing fell, Emperor Yuan of Liang pitied the slaughter of his household and specially enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yuanxiang with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 僧辯為司徒，以炯為從事中郎。

translations.literal: When Sengbian became Minister of Education, he made Jiong a retainer in his secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Sengbian became minister of education he made Jiong a secretariat retainer.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝徵為給事黃門侍郎，領尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang summoned him as Attendant of the Yellow Gate in the Secretariat and concurrent Left Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan summoned him as attendant of the yellow gate and concurrent left director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 荊州陷，為西魏所虜，魏人甚禮之，授炯儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Jingzhou fell he was captured by Western Wei; the Wei people treated him with great courtesy and appointed Jiong Palace Attendant of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzhou fell he was taken by Western Wei. They honored him and made him palace attendant of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 炯以母老在東，恆思歸國，恐魏人愛其文才而留之，恆閉門卻掃，無所交遊。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old in the east, Jiong constantly longed to return home, fearing the Wei would love his literary talent and detain him; he always shut his gate and swept no visitors, having no social ties.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was old in the east and he longed to go home, fearing the Wei would keep him for his writing. He shut his gate, swept away callers, and kept no company.

sentences.zh: 時有文章，隨即棄毀，不令流布。

translations.literal: Whenever he had writings he at once destroyed them and would not let them circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever he wrote he destroyed at once and would not let it spread.

sentences.zh: 嘗獨行經漢武通天臺，為表奏之，陳己思歸之意。

translations.literal: Once, walking alone past Emperor Wu of Han's Tower of Reaching Heaven, he submitted a memorial stating his wish to return.
translations.idiomatic: Once he walked alone past the Han Tower of Reaching Heaven and submitted a memorial pleading to return.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：「臣聞喬山雖掩，鼎湖之靈可祠，有魯既荒，大庭之跡無泯。

translations.literal: The text says: "Your servant has heard that though Qiao Mountain is covered over, the spirit of the Tripod Lake may still be worshipped; though Youlu is waste, the traces of the Great Court are not lost.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "I have heard that though Qiao Mountain is buried, the spirit at Tripod Lake may still be honored; though Youlu lies waste, the Great Court's traces are not gone.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下降德猗蘭，纂靈豐谷。

translations.literal: I bow before Your Majesty's descending virtue like the orchid on the slope, your gathering of numinous power in the rich valley.
translations.idiomatic: I bow before Your Majesty's grace descending like orchids on the slope, your gathering of numinous power in the rich valley.

sentences.zh: 漢道既登，神仙可望，射之罘於海浦，禮日觀而稱功，橫中流於汾河，指柏梁而高宴，何其樂也，豈不然歟！

translations.literal: When Han's Way had ascended, immortals could be hoped for; shooting the zhi at the sea shore, performing rites at Sun Terrace and proclaiming merit, crossing midstream on the Fen River, pointing to Cypress Beam and feasting high—what joy, is it not so!
translations.idiomatic: When Han's Way had risen, immortals seemed near: shooting zhi at the sea shore, rites at Sun Terrace proclaiming merit, crossing midstream on the Fen, feasting high at Cypress Beam—what joy, was it not so!

sentences.zh: 既而運屬上仙，道窮晏駕，甲帳珠簾，一朝零落，茂陵玉碗，宛出人間，陵雲故基，共原田而膴膴，別風餘

translations.literal: Then fortune turned to the transcendent lord, the Way reached the imperial carriage's halt; armored curtains and pearl blinds fell in a morning; the jade bowl of Maoling came forth among men; the old base of Lingyun shared the open fields in lush growth; the separate wind's remnant
translations.idiomatic: Then fate turned to the transcendent lord and the imperial carriage halted; armored curtains and pearl blinds fell in a morning; Maoling's jade bowl walked among men; Lingyun's old base turned to lush open fields; the remnant of the separate wind

translations.literal: (toe)
translations.idiomatic: (toe)

sentences.zh: 〔 址〕，[2]對陵阜而茫茫，羇旅縲臣，能不落淚。

translations.literal: [site], Editorial footnote marker 2. facing the tomb mound in boundless expanse—a captive minister in bonds, how could he not shed tears?
translations.idiomatic: [site], [2] facing the tomb mounds in boundless haze—a captive minister in bonds, how could tears not fall?

sentences.zh: 昔承明既厭，嚴助東歸，駟馬可乘，長卿西返，恭聞故實，竊有愚心。

translations.literal: In old days when Chenming was weary, Yan Zhu returned east; four-horse carriages could be taken, Sima Xiangru came back west—I respectfully hear these precedents and secretly harbor this foolish wish.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenming grew weary, Yan Zhu went east; four-horse carriages waited, Sima Xiangru returned west—I hear these precedents and harbor this foolish wish.

sentences.zh: 黍稷非馨，敢忘徼福。

translations.literal: Though millet and millet are not fragrant, I dare not forget to seek blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Though the offering lacks fragrance, I dare not forget to seek blessing.

sentences.zh: 」奏訖，其夜炯夢見有宮禁之所，兵衛甚嚴，炯便以情事陳訴，聞有人言：「甚不惜放卿還，幾時可至。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was finished, that night Jiong dreamed of a place within the palace precincts where guards were very strict; he stated his case, and heard someone say: "We are quite willing to let you return—when may you arrive?"
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was done, that night he dreamed of palace precincts under strict guard. He pleaded his case and heard a voice: "We are quite willing to let you go home—when will you arrive?"

sentences.zh: 」少日，便與王克等並獲東歸。

translations.literal: " Within a few days he and Wang Ke and others were all able to return east.
translations.idiomatic: " Within days he and Wang Ke and others were all sent home to the east.

sentences.zh: 紹泰二年至都，除司農卿，遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaotai he reached the capital and was made Director of the Directorate of Agriculture, then transferred to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaotai year 2 (555) he reached the capital, was made director of the directorate of agriculture, then censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，加通直散騎常侍，中丞如故。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, Jiong was given the added post of Regular Attendant for Direct Communication, censor-in-chief unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne he was given the added post of regular attendant for direct communication while keeping the censorate.

sentences.zh: 以母老表請歸養，詔不許。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old he memorialized asking to return and support her; an edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to go home and tend his aged mother; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 文帝嗣位，又表曰：「臣嬰生不幸，弱冠而孤，母子零丁，兄弟相長。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded he again memorialized, saying: "Your servant from infancy met misfortune; at twenty he was orphaned; mother and son were alone, brothers raised one another.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded he memorialized again: "From infancy I met misfortune. At twenty I was orphaned; mother and son were alone, brothers raised each other.

sentences.zh: 謹身為養，仕不擇官，宦成梁朝，命存亂世，冒危履險，

translations.literal: I kept my person to support them, took office without choosing rank, served to completion under Liang, my life preserved in chaotic times, braving danger and treading peril,
translations.idiomatic: I kept my body to nourish them, took any office, served Liang to the end, and lived through chaos, braving danger at every step,

translations.literal: (self)
translations.idiomatic: (self)

sentences.zh: 〔百〕死輕生，[3]妻息誅夷，昆季冥滅，餘臣母子，得逢興運。

translations.literal: [hundred] deaths counted light, Editorial footnote marker 3. wife and children executed, brothers extinguished; your servant and his mother alone met the rising fortune.
translations.idiomatic: [hundred] deaths counted light, [3] wife and children slain, brothers gone; only your servant and his mother met this rising fortune.

sentences.zh: 臣母妾劉，今年八十有一，臣叔母妾丘，七十有五，臣門弟姪故自無人，妾丘兒孫又久亡泯，兩家侍養，餘臣一人。

translations.literal: Your servant's mother, concubine Liu, is this year eighty-one; your servant's uncle's wife, concubine Qiu, is seventy-five; your servant's younger brothers and nephews in the clan are gone, and concubine Qiu's grandsons long since perished—of the two households to be served, only your servant remains.
translations.idiomatic: My mother, Lady Liu, is eighty-one; my uncle's wife, Lady Qiu, is seventy-five. Our younger kin are gone and Lady Qiu's grandsons are long dead—of the two households that must be served, only I remain.

sentences.zh: 前帝知臣之孤煢，養臣以州里，不欲使頓居草萊，又復矜臣溫凊，所以一年之內，再三休沐。

translations.literal: The former emperor knew your servant's loneliness, nourished him with a post in his home district, and did not wish him to dwell suddenly in the wilds; he again pitied your servant's warmth in winter and cool in summer, so within one year he granted leave again and again.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor knew my desolation, kept me in a post near home, and would not leave me in the wild; he pitied my duty to warm and cool my elders, and within a year granted leave again and again.

sentences.zh: 臣之屢披丹款，頻冒宸鑒，非欲苟違朝廷，遠離畿輦。

translations.literal: Your servant's repeated laying bare of his loyal heart and frequent braving of the imperial gaze were not from wishing to defy the court or leave the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: I laid my heart bare again and again and braved the throne's gaze—not because I wished to defy the court or flee the capital.

sentences.zh: 一者以年將六十，湯火居心，每跪讀家書，前懼後喜，溫枕扇席，無復成童。

translations.literal: First, as the years approach sixty, boiling water sits in the heart; whenever kneeling to read a letter from home, fear comes before and joy after; warming the pillow and fanning the mat—no longer the ways of childhood.
translations.idiomatic: First, nearing sixty, my heart is scalding water; each time I kneel to a letter from home, fear comes first and joy after; to warm the pillow and fan the mat is no longer the work of a child.

sentences.zh: 二者職居彝憲，邦之司直，若自虧身禮，[4]何問國章？

translations.literal: Second, the office holds the imperial statutes—the state's straightedge; if one himself impairs the rites of the body, Editorial footnote marker 4. how may one inquire into the nation's laws?
translations.idiomatic: Second, my post holds the imperial statutes—the state's straightedge; if I impair my own filial duty, [4] how may I judge the nation's laws?

sentences.zh: 前德綢繆，始許哀放，內侍近臣，多悉此旨。

translations.literal: Former grace was close and at first allowed compassionate release; inner attendants and close ministers mostly knew this intent.
translations.idiomatic: Former grace was close and at first promised compassionate release; inner attendants and close ministers knew that intent.

sentences.zh: 正以選賢與能，廣求明哲，趦趄荏苒，未始取才。

translations.literal: It was only because in choosing the worthy and employing the able, widely seeking the wise and clear, I hesitated and delayed and had not yet taken talent.
translations.idiomatic: Only because in choosing the worthy and seeking the wise I hesitated and delayed, and had not yet yielded my post.

sentences.zh: 而上玄降戾，奄至今日，德音在耳，墳土遽乾，悠悠昊天，哀此罔極。

translations.literal: Yet High Heaven sent down affliction and suddenly it reached today; the virtuous voice is still in the ear, the grave earth is already dry—vast is August Heaven, pity this boundless grief.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Heaven sent down affliction and suddenly it is today; his gracious voice is still in my ear, the grave earth already dry—vast Heaven, pity this boundless grief.

sentences.zh: 兼臣私心煎切，彌迫近時，慺慺之祈，轉忘塵觸。

translations.literal: Together with your servant's private heart seared and pressed, ever nearer in time, his earnest prayer forgets even dust on his robe.
translations.idiomatic: Together with my private heart seared and pressed, ever nearer in time, earnest prayer forgets even the dust on my robe.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下睿哲聰明，嗣興下武，刑于四海，弘此孝治。

translations.literal: I bow before Your Majesty's wise clarity and intelligence, succeeding and raising martial virtue, taking punishment as model for the four seas and spreading this filial governance.
translations.idiomatic: I bow before Your Majesty's wise clarity, raising martial virtue in succession, taking punishment as model for the four seas and spreading this filial rule.

sentences.zh: 寸管求天，仰歸帷扆，有感必應，實望聖明。

translations.literal: With an inch of brush I seek Heaven, looking up to return within the curtain; where there is feeling there must be response—I truly look to sagely clarity.
translations.idiomatic: With an inch of brush I seek Heaven, looking up to return within the curtain; where feeling moves, response must come—I trust in sagely clarity.

sentences.zh: 特乞霈然申其私禮，則王者之德，覃及無方，矧彼翔沈，孰非涵養。

translations.literal: I specially beg that you grant in full my private rites; then the kingly virtue will reach without limit—how much more those who soar and sink, who are not all nurtured?
translations.idiomatic: I beg that you grant my private rites in full; then kingly virtue reaches without limit—how much more those who soar and sink, who are not all nurtured?

sentences.zh: 」詔答曰：「省表具懷。

translations.literal: " The edict replied: "I have read your memorial and take your meaning.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict replied: "Your memorial is received and your meaning understood.

sentences.zh: 卿譽馳咸、雒，情深宛、沛。

translations.literal: Your fame has raced through Xianyang and Luoyang; your feeling runs deep as Wan and Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Your fame has raced through Xianyang and Luoyang; your feeling runs deep as Wan and Pei.

sentences.zh: 日者理切倚門，[5]言歸異域，復牽時役，遂乖侍養。

translations.literal: Lately reason pressed at the leaning door, Editorial footnote marker 5. words turned toward a foreign land; again bound by timely service, you missed attending them.
translations.idiomatic: Lately reason pressed at the leaning door, [5] words turned toward a foreign land; again bound by timely service, you missed attending them.

sentences.zh: 雖周生之思，每欲棄官，戴禮垂文，得遺從政，前朝光宅四海，劬勞萬機，以卿才為獨步，職居專席，方深委任，屢屈情禮。

translations.literal: Though Zhou Sheng's thought each time wished to abandon office, Dai Li's handed-down text allowed leaving office to follow policy; the former court's glory filled the four seas and toiled at the myriad affairs of state—because your talent stood alone, your office held the special mat, and just as deep trust was placed, again and again feeling and rites were bent.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhou Sheng's thought each time wished to quit office, Dai Li's handed-down text allowed leaving office for policy; the former court's glory filled the four seas and toiled at myriad affairs—because your talent stood alone, your office held the special mat, and just as trust deepened, again and again feeling and rites were bent.

sentences.zh: 朕嗣奉洪基，思弘景業，顧茲寡薄，兼纏哀疚，實賴賢哲，同致雍熙，豈便釋簡南闈，解紱東路。

translations.literal: I now succeed to the great foundation, thinking to spread the splendid enterprise; looking on this meager thinness and also wound with mourning grief, I truly rely on the worthy and wise to bring harmony together—how could I lightly set aside the southern ministries and unfasten the eastern road?
translations.idiomatic: I now succeed to the great foundation and think to spread the splendid enterprise; looking on my meager worth and wound with mourning, I truly rely on the worthy to bring harmony—how could I lightly set aside the southern ministries and unfasten the eastern road?

sentences.zh: 當今馮親入舍，荀母從官，用睹朝榮，不虧家禮。

translations.literal: Today Feng Qin entered the house and Xun's mother followed the office—you may see court glory without impairing family rites.
translations.idiomatic: Today Feng Qin entered the house and Xun's mother followed the office—you may see court glory without impairing family rites.

sentences.zh: 尋敕所由，相迎尊累，使卿公私得所，並無廢也。」

translations.literal: Soon I shall order the responsible offices to welcome your honored kin, so that you may have what is fitting in public and private, and nothing will be neglected."
translations.idiomatic: Soon I shall order the responsible offices to welcome your honored kin, so that public and private needs are met, and nothing neglected."

sentences.zh: 初，高祖嘗稱炯宜居王佐，軍國大政，多預謀謨，文帝又重其才用，欲寵貴之。

translations.literal: Earlier the Founder had said Jiong was fit for a king's assistant; in great affairs of army and state he took part in many plans; Emperor Wen again valued his talent and wished to honor him richly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Founder had said Jiong was fit for a king's assistant; in army and state he took part in many plans; Emperor Wen again valued his talent and wished to honor him richly.

sentences.zh: 會王琳入寇大雷，留異擁據東境，帝欲使炯因是立功，乃解中丞，加明威將軍，遣還鄉里，收合徒眾。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Lin invaded Dalei and Liu Yi held the eastern marches; the emperor wished to have Jiong win merit thereby, so relieved him as censor-in-chief, gave him the added title General of Bright Prestige, and sent him back to his home district to gather followers.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lin invaded Dalei and Liu Yi held the eastern marches, the emperor wished Jiong to win merit thereby, relieved him as censor-in-chief, made him general of bright prestige, and sent him home to gather followers.

sentences.zh: 以疾卒于吳中，時年五十九。

translations.literal: He died of illness in Wu, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in Wu, aged fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 文帝聞之，即日舉哀，并遣弔祭，贈侍中，諡曰恭子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen heard it he at once went into mourning and also sent condolences; he was posthumously made Palace Attendant, posthumous name Gongzi.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen heard it he mourned that same day and sent condolences; he was posthumously made palace attendant, posthumous name Gongzi.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷行於世。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in twenty rolls circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: A collected works in twenty rolls circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 虞荔字山披，會稽餘姚人也。

translations.literal: Yu Li, styled Shanpi, was a native of Yuyao in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Li, styled Shanpi, came from Yuyao in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 祖權，梁廷尉卿、永嘉太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Quan was Minister of Justice under Liang and Administrator of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Quan was Liang's minister of justice and administrator of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 父檢，平北始興王諮議參軍。

translations.literal: His father Jian was a staff adviser to the Prince of Shixing, Pacifier of the North.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jian was a staff adviser to the Prince of Shixing, pacifier of the north.

sentences.zh: 荔幼聰敏，有志操。

translations.literal: Li in youth was clever and keen, with will and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Li was clever and keen in youth, with firm will and conduct.

sentences.zh: 年九歲，隨從伯闡候太常陸倕，倕問五經凡有十事，荔隨問輒應，無有遺失，倕甚異之。

translations.literal: At age nine he followed his father's elder brother Kan to call on the Minister of Rites Lu Yan; Yan asked ten matters on the Five Classics and Li answered each question as asked, missing nothing—Yan marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he followed his father's elder brother Kan to call on Minister of Rites Lu Yan. Yan asked ten points on the Five Classics; Li answered each without miss, and Yan marveled.

sentences.zh: 又嘗詣徵士何胤，時太守衡陽王亦造焉，胤言之於王，王欲見荔，荔辭曰：「未有板刺，無容拜謁。

translations.literal: He also once visited the recluse He Yin; at the time the Administrator, the Prince of Hengyang, also came, and Yin spoke of him to the prince; the prince wished to see Li, but Li declined, saying: "I have no visiting tablet and cannot pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: He once visited the recluse He Yin. The Prince of Hengyang, then administrator, also came; Yin spoke of Li to the prince, who wished to see him. Li declined: "I have no visiting tablet and cannot pay respects.

sentences.zh: 」王以荔有高尚之志，雅相欽重，還郡，即辟為主簿，荔又辭以年小不就。

translations.literal: " The prince, because Li had lofty aims, honored him deeply; returning to his commandery he at once summoned him as chief clerk, but Li again declined on grounds of youth and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince, seeing Li's lofty aims, honored him deeply. Back in his commandery he summoned Li as chief clerk; Li again declined as too young.

sentences.zh: 及長，美風儀，博覽墳籍，善屬文。

translations.literal: When grown he had fine bearing, broadly read the classics, and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he had fine bearing, read broadly in the classics, and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 釋褐梁西中郎行參軍，尋署法曹外兵參軍，兼丹陽詔獄正。

translations.literal: He doffed the commoner's garb as a traveling aide in Liang's Western Central Commandery, soon was appointed Outer Army Major in the Law Office, and concurrently Chief of the Danyang Imperial Prison.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a traveling aide in Liang's western central commandery, soon as outer-army major in the law office and concurrent chief of the Danyang imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝於城西置士林館，荔乃製碑，奏上，帝命勒之于館，仍用荔為士林學士。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang set up the Forest of Scholars Hall west of the city; Li composed a stele, submitted it, and the emperor ordered it carved in the hall and still employed Li as a Forest of Scholars academician.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang set up the Forest of Scholars west of the city. Li composed a stele and submitted it; the emperor had it carved in the hall and made Li an academician there.

sentences.zh: 尋為司文郎，遷通直散騎侍郎，兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Editorial Officer of Writings, transferred to Regular Attendant for Direct Communication, and concurrently Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was editorial officer of writings, then regular attendant for direct communication and concurrent secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 時左右之任，多參權軸，內外機務，互有帶掌，唯荔與顧協淡然靖退，居于西省，但以文史見知，當時號為清白。

translations.literal: At the time those in close attendance mostly shared in the power axis; inner and outer affairs were each partly held—only Li and Gu Xie were calm, retiring, and dwelt in the Western Secretariat, known only through literature and history; the age called them pure.
translations.idiomatic: Close attendants then mostly shared the power axis; inner and outer affairs were split among them—only Li and Gu Xie stayed calm and retired in the western secretariat, known for literature and history; the age called them pure.

sentences.zh: 尋領大著作。

translations.literal: Soon he headed the Grand Institute for Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he headed the grand institute for writing.

sentences.zh: 及侯景之亂，荔率親屬入臺，除鎮西諮議參軍，舍人如故。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, Li led kin into the Terrace City and was made Staff Adviser to the Pacifier of the West, secretariat gentleman unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled Li led kin into the Terrace City and was made staff adviser to the pacifier of the west, secretariat gentleman unchanged.

sentences.zh: 臺城陷，逃歸鄉里。

translations.literal: When the Terrace City fell he fled home.
translations.idiomatic: When the Terrace City fell he fled home.

sentences.zh: 侯景平，元帝徵為中書侍郎，貞陽侯，授揚州別駕，並不就。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, Emperor Yuan summoned him as Secretariat Gentleman and Marquis of Zhenyang, and appointed him Vice Governor of Yangzhou—all of which he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing fell, Emperor Yuan summoned him as secretariat gentleman and Marquis of Zhenyang and made him vice governor of Yangzhou; he accepted none of it.

sentences.zh: 張彪之據會稽也，荔時在焉。

translations.literal: When Zhang Biao held Kuaiji, Li was there.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Biao held Kuaiji, Li was there.

sentences.zh: 及文帝平彪，高祖遺荔書曰：「喪亂已來，賢哲凋散，君才用有美，聲聞許、洛，當今朝廷惟新，廣求英雋，豈可栖遲東土，獨善其身？

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen pacified Biao, the Founder sent Li a letter saying: "Since the mourning and chaos, worthies have scattered; your talent and use are fine, your fame heard in Xu and Luo; today's court is newly ordered and widely seeks heroes—how can you linger in the eastern lands and keep goodness to yourself?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen pacified Biao, the Founder wrote: "Since the chaos, worthies have scattered. Your talent is fine and your fame heard in Xu and Luo. The court is newly ordered and seeks heroes widely—how can you linger in the east and keep goodness to yourself?

sentences.zh: 今令兄子將接出都，想必副朝廷虛遲也。

translations.literal: I now order your elder brother's son to come out and meet you in the capital; surely you will answer the court's eager waiting.
translations.idiomatic: I now order your elder brother's son to bring you to the capital; surely you will answer the court's eager waiting.

sentences.zh: 」文帝又與書曰：「君東南有美，聲譽洽聞，自應翰飛京許，共康時弊，而

translations.literal: " Emperor Wen also wrote: "You have beauty in the southeast, fame that spreads; you should yourself brush the capital and Xu, together set right the age's ills, yet
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Wen also wrote: "You have beauty in the southeast and fame that spreads; you should brush the capital and Xu and set right the age's ills, yet

translations.literal: (cut)
translations.idiomatic: (cut)

sentences.zh: 〔削〕跡丘園，[6]保茲獨善，豈使稱空谷之望邪？

translations.literal: [pared] your traces in gardens and fields, Editorial footnote marker 6. keeping this solitary goodness—will you let the empty valley's hope be spoken in vain?
translations.idiomatic: [pared] your traces in gardens and fields, [6] keeping solitary goodness—will you let the empty valley's hope be spoken in vain?

sentences.zh: 必願便爾俶裝，且為出都之計。

translations.literal: I surely wish you at once to pack and also make plans to leave for the capital.
translations.idiomatic: I surely wish you to pack at once and plan to leave for the capital.

sentences.zh: 唯遲披覯，在於茲日。

translations.literal: I only wait to see you—may that day be soon.
translations.idiomatic: I only wait to see you—may that day be soon.

sentences.zh: 」迫切之不得已，乃應命至都。

translations.literal: " Pressed urgently and with no way out, he then answered the summons and reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: " Pressed urgently and with no way out, he answered the summons and reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩，文帝嗣位，除太子中庶子，仍侍太子讀書。

translations.literal: When the Founder died and Emperor Wen succeeded, Li was made Crown Prince Attendant and still attended the crown prince in study.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder died and Emperor Wen succeeded, Li was made crown prince attendant and still tutored the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 尋領大著作、東揚揚州二州大中正，庶子如故。

translations.literal: Soon he headed the Grand Institute for Writing and was Grand Arbiter for the two provinces of East Yang and Yangzhou, attendant unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he headed the grand institute for writing and was grand arbiter for East Yang and Yangzhou, attendant unchanged.

sentences.zh: 初，荔母隨荔入臺，卒於臺內，尋而城陷，情禮不申，由是終身蔬食布衣，不聽音樂，雖任遇隆重，而居止儉素，淡然無營。

translations.literal: Earlier Li's mother had followed Li into the Terrace City and died within it; soon the city fell and feeling and rites could not be observed—therefore for life he ate vegetables and wore plain cloth, heard no music; though his appointment was weighty, his dwelling was spare and he had no designs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier his mother had followed him into the Terrace City and died there; soon the city fell and rites could not be observed—therefore for life he ate vegetables and plain cloth and heard no music; though honored in office, his dwelling was spare and he had no designs.

sentences.zh: 文帝深器之，常引在左右，朝夕顧訪。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen valued him deeply, constantly kept him at hand, and morning and evening sought his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen valued him deeply, kept him at hand, and morning and evening sought his counsel.

sentences.zh: 荔性沉密，少言論，凡所獻替，莫有見其際者，故不列于後焉。

translations.literal: Li by nature was deep and close, seldom spoke in debate; whatever he offered in counsel, none saw its inner workings—therefore he is not listed in what follows.
translations.idiomatic: Li by nature was deep and close, seldom debated; whatever he offered in counsel none saw its inner workings—therefore he is not listed in what follows.

sentences.zh: 時荔第二弟寄寓於閩中，依陳寶應，荔每言之輒流涕。

translations.literal: At the time Li's second younger brother Ji was staying in Min, relying on Chen Baoying; whenever Li spoke of it he wept.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li's second younger brother Ji was staying in Min under Chen Baoying; whenever Li spoke of it he wept.

sentences.zh: 文帝哀而謂曰：「我亦有弟在遠，此情甚切，他人豈知。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen pitied him and said: "I too have a brother far away; this feeling is very keen—how would others know?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen pitied him and said: "I too have a brother far away; this feeling is keen—how would others know?

sentences.zh: 」乃敕寶應求寄，寶應終不遣。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Baoying to send Ji back, but Baoying in the end did not send him.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered Baoying to send Ji back, but Baoying never sent him.

sentences.zh: 荔因以感疾，帝數往臨視。

translations.literal: Li thereby fell ill with grief; the emperor several times went in person to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: Li fell ill with grief; the emperor visited him in person several times.

sentences.zh: 令荔將家口入省，荔以禁中非私居之所，乞停城外，文帝不許，乃令住於蘭臺，乘輿再三臨問，手敕中使，相望於道。

translations.literal: He ordered Li to bring his household into the Secretariat; Li said the forbidden precinct was no private dwelling and begged to stop outside the walls; Emperor Wen did not permit it and had him stay at Orchid Terrace; the imperial carriage again and again visited him in person; hand-edicts and inner envoys lined the road.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Li to bring his household into the secretariat; Li said the forbidden precinct was no private home and begged to stay outside the walls. Emperor Wen refused and had him stay at Orchid Terrace; the imperial carriage visited again and again; hand-edicts and inner envoys lined the road.

sentences.zh: 又以荔蔬食積久，非羸疾所堪，乃敕曰：「能敦布素，乃當為高，卿年事已多，氣力稍減，方欲仗委，良須克壯，今給卿魚肉，不得固從所執也。

translations.literal: Also, because Li's vegetable diet had long continued and was not what a wasting illness could bear, an edict said: "To be able to keep plain cloth is indeed lofty; you are already advanced in years and your strength has somewhat declined—just when I wish to rely on you, I truly need you hale; I now give you fish and meat—you must not stubbornly follow what you have held to.
translations.idiomatic: Because Li's vegetable diet had long continued and was not what a wasting illness could bear, an edict said: "To keep plain cloth is indeed lofty; you are advanced in years and your strength has declined—just when I wish to rely on you I need you hale; I now give you fish and meat—you must not stubbornly hold to your vow.

sentences.zh: 」荔終不從。

translations.literal: " Li in the end did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: " Li in the end did not obey.

sentences.zh: 天嘉二年卒，時年五十九。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng he died, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancheng year 2 (561) he died, aged fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 文帝甚傷惜之，贈侍中，諡曰德子。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen grieved deeply, posthumously made him Palace Attendant, posthumous name Dezi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen grieved deeply, posthumously made him palace attendant, posthumous name Dezi.

sentences.zh: 及喪柩還鄉里，上親出臨送，當時榮之。

translations.literal: When the coffin returned to his home district the emperor went out in person to see him off—the age counted it glory.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin returned home the emperor went out in person to see him off—the age counted it glory.

sentences.zh: 子世基、世南，並少知名。

translations.literal: His sons Shiji and Shinan were both known in youth.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Shiji and Shinan were both known in youth.

sentences.zh: 寄字次安，少聰敏。

translations.literal: Ji, styled Ci'an, was clever in youth.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, styled Ci'an, was clever in youth.

sentences.zh: 年數歲，客有造其父者，遇寄於門，因嘲之曰︰「郎君姓虞，必當無智。

translations.literal: When a few years old, a guest came to visit his father and met Ji at the gate; he therefore mocked him, saying: "Young master, your surname is Yu—you must surely have no wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: When a few years old a guest came to his father and met Ji at the gate. He mocked him: "Young master, your surname is Yu—you must have no wisdom.

sentences.zh: 」寄應聲答曰：「文字不辨，豈得非愚？

translations.literal: " Ji answered on the spot: "If you cannot tell the characters, are you not foolish?
translations.idiomatic: " Ji answered at once: "If you cannot tell the characters, are you not foolish?

sentences.zh: 」客大慚。

translations.literal: " The guest was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: " The guest was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 入謂其父曰：「此子非常人，文舉之對不是過也。」

translations.literal: Entering he said to Ji's father: "This child is no ordinary person—Wenju's reply was not better than this."
translations.idiomatic: Entering, he told Ji's father: "This child is no ordinary person—Wenju's reply was not better."

sentences.zh: 及長，好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: When grown he loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he loved learning and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 性沖靜，有栖遁之志。

translations.literal: By nature he was mild and still, with the will to dwell in seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was mild and still and wished to dwell in seclusion.

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉秀才，對策高第。

translations.literal: At twenty he was recommended as a cultivated talent and in the policy response ranked high.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he was recommended as cultivated talent and ranked high in the policy response.

sentences.zh: 起家梁宣城王國左常侍。

translations.literal: He began his career as Left Regular Attendant in the Kingdom of Xuan[cheng] under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He began as left regular attendant in Liang's Kingdom of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 大同中，嘗驟雨，殿前往往有雜色寶珠，梁武觀之甚有喜色，寄因上瑞雨頌。

translations.literal: In the Datong era, once in a sudden rain, before the hall there were often mixed-colored precious pearls; Emperor Wu of Liang viewed them with great pleasure, and Ji therefore submitted a eulogy on the auspicious rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the Datong era a sudden rain once left mixed-colored pearls before the hall. Emperor Wu of Liang was greatly pleased, and Ji submitted a eulogy on the auspicious rain.

sentences.zh: 帝謂寄兄荔曰：「此頌典裁清拔，卿家之士龍也。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Ji's elder brother Li: "This eulogy's style is clear and lofty—your family's Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Ji's elder brother Li: "This eulogy is clear and lofty—your family's Shilong.

sentences.zh: 將如何擢用？

translations.literal: How will you promote and employ him?
translations.idiomatic: How will you promote and employ him?

sentences.zh: 」寄聞之，歎曰：「美盛德之形容，以申擊壤之情耳。

translations.literal: " When Ji heard it he sighed: "To praise the flourishing virtue's form is only to voice the joy of beating clods.
translations.idiomatic: " When Ji heard it he sighed: "To praise flourishing virtue is only to voice the joy of beating clods.

sentences.zh: 吾豈買名求仕者乎？

translations.literal: Am I one who buys a name to seek office?
translations.idiomatic: Am I one who buys a name to seek office?

sentences.zh: 」乃閉門稱疾，唯以書籍自娛。

translations.literal: " He then shut his door and claimed illness, taking only books for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: " He shut his door and claimed illness, taking only books for pleasure.

sentences.zh: 岳陽王為會稽太守，引寄為行參軍，遷記室參軍，領郡五官掾。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yueyang was Administrator of Kuaiji he brought in Ji as a traveling aide, transferred him to Staff Recorder, and had him lead the commandery's Five Offices Major.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yueyang was administrator of Kuaiji he brought Ji in as traveling aide, then staff recorder, leading the commandery's five offices major.

sentences.zh: 又轉中記室，掾如故。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Central Staff Recorder, major unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made central staff recorder, major unchanged.

sentences.zh: 在職簡略煩苛，務存大體，曹局之內，終日寂然。

translations.literal: In office he was brief with troublesome detail, keeping to the great body; within the bureau all day was silence.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was brief with troublesome detail and kept to the great body; within the bureau all day was silence.

sentences.zh: 及寶應結婚留異，潛有逆謀，寄微知其意，言說之際，每陳逆順之理，微以諷諫，寶應輒引說他事以拒之。

translations.literal: When Baoying allied by marriage with Liu Yi he secretly harbored rebellious designs; Ji faintly knew his intent and in conversation always stated the logic of obedience and rebellion, subtly admonishing; Baoying always turned to other matters to refuse.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoying allied by marriage with Liu Yi he secretly harbored rebellion; Ji faintly knew it and in talk always stated the logic of obedience and rebellion, subtly admonishing; Baoying always turned to other matters.

sentences.zh: 又嘗令左右誦漢書，臥而聽之，至蒯通說韓信曰「相君之背，貴不可言」，寶應蹶然起曰「可謂智士」。

translations.literal: He also once had attendants recite the Book of Han while he lay listening; when it reached Kuai Tong telling Han Xin "I see your back—nobility beyond words," Baoying started up and said "He may be called a wise man."
translations.idiomatic: He once had attendants recite the Book of Han while he listened lying down. At Kuai Tong telling Han Xin "I see your back—nobility beyond words," Baoying started up: "He may be called wise."

sentences.zh: 寄正色曰：「覆酈驕韓，未足稱智；

translations.literal: Ji with stern countenance said: "Overturning Li and insulting Han is not enough to be called wisdom;
translations.idiomatic: Ji said sternly: "Overturning Li and insulting Han is not enough to be called wisdom;

sentences.zh: 豈若班彪王命，識所歸乎？」

translations.literal: how does it compare with Ban Biao's Mandate of Kings, knowing where to turn?"
translations.idiomatic: how does it compare with Ban Biao's Mandate of Kings, knowing where to turn?"

sentences.zh: 寄知寶應不可諫，慮禍及己，乃為居士服以拒絕之。

translations.literal: Ji knew Baoying could not be admonished and feared disaster reaching himself; he therefore wore lay believer's robes to refuse him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji knew Baoying could not be admonished and feared disaster; he wore lay believer's robes to refuse him.

sentences.zh: 常居東山寺，偽稱腳疾，不復起，寶應以為假託，使燒寄所臥屋，寄安臥不動。

translations.literal: He constantly dwelt at East Mountain Temple, falsely claiming foot ailment and not rising again; Baoying thought it pretense and had Ji's sleeping house burned; Ji lay at ease and did not move.
translations.idiomatic: He dwelt at East Mountain Temple, falsely claiming foot ailment and not rising; Baoying thought it pretense and burned Ji's sleeping house; Ji lay still.

sentences.zh: 親近將扶寄出，寄曰：「吾命有所懸，避欲安往？

translations.literal: Close kin were about to help Ji out; Ji said: "My fate has something it hangs on—where would fleeing go?
translations.idiomatic: Kin were about to help him out; Ji said: "My fate has something it hangs on—where would fleeing go?

sentences.zh: 」所縱火者，旋自救之。

translations.literal: " Those who had set the fire at once themselves put it out.
translations.idiomatic: " Those who set the fire at once put it out themselves.

sentences.zh: 寶應自此方信。

translations.literal: From this Baoying then believed.
translations.idiomatic: From this Baoying then believed.

sentences.zh: 及留異稱兵，寶應資其部曲，寄乃因書極諫曰：

translations.literal: When Liu Yi raised troops Baoying supplied his command; Ji therefore by letter admonished to the utmost, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yi raised troops Baoying supplied his command; Ji therefore wrote a letter admonishing to the utmost:

sentences.zh: 東山虞寄致書於明將軍使君節下：寄流離世故，飄寓貴鄉，將軍待以上賓之禮，申以國士之眷，意氣所感，何日忘之。

translations.literal: Yu Ji of East Mountain sends a letter to the Bright General, Lord and Envoy: Ji, adrift through worldly change, sojourns in your honored district; the general treated him with the rites of a chief guest and extended the affection due a state's scholar—the feeling stirred, what day could it be forgotten!
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ji of East Mountain to the Bright General, Lord and Envoy: Adrift through worldly change, I sojourn in your honored district. You treated me with a chief guest's rites and a state's scholar's affection—what day could that feeling be forgotten!

sentences.zh: 而寄沈痼彌留，愒陰將盡，常恐卒填溝壑，涓塵莫報，是以敢布腹心，冒陳丹款，願將軍留須臾之慮，少思察之，則瞑目之日，所懷畢矣。

translations.literal: Yet Ji's deep illness lingers on, the setting sun nearly spent; I constantly fear I may suddenly fill a ditch and moat and repay not even a drop of dust—therefore I dare lay bare my inmost heart and risk stating my loyal red; I wish the general would pause a moment's thought and reflect a little—then on the day eyes close, what is in the breast would be complete.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my deep illness lingers, the setting sun nearly spent; I constantly fear I may fill a ditch and repay not even a drop—therefore I dare lay bare my heart and risk my loyal red. Pause a moment's thought and reflect a little—then on the day my eyes close, what is in my breast would be complete.

sentences.zh: 夫安危之兆，禍福之機，匪獨天時，[7]亦由人事。

translations.literal: The omens of safety and danger, the mechanisms of fortune and calamity, are not only Heaven's seasons, Editorial footnote marker 7. but also lie in human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The omens of safety and danger, the mechanisms of fortune and calamity, are not only Heaven's seasons, [7] but also lie in human affairs.

sentences.zh: 失之毫釐，差以千里。

translations.literal: To miss by a hair's breadth is to err by a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Miss by a hair's breadth and err by a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 是以明智之士，據重位而不傾，執大節而不失，豈惑於浮辭哉？

translations.literal: Therefore the wise man holds heavy position without toppling, grasps great integrity without losing it—how would he be deluded by floating words?
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the wise hold heavy position without toppling, grasp great integrity without losing it—how would they be deluded by floating words?

sentences.zh: 將軍文武兼資，英威不世，往因多難，杖劍興師，援旗誓眾，抗威千里，豈不以四郊多壘，共謀王室，匡時報主，寧國庇民乎？

translations.literal: The general combines civil and martial gifts, his heroic prestige unmatched in the age; in former days through many hardships you took sword and raised troops, lifted the banner and swore the host, resisted prestige a thousand li—was it not because the four suburbs had many ramparts and together you plotted for the royal house, set the age right and repaid the lord, settled the state and sheltered the people?
translations.idiomatic: You combine civil and martial gifts, heroic prestige unmatched in the age; in former days through hardship you took sword and raised troops, lifted the banner and swore the host, resisted prestige a thousand li—was it not because the four suburbs had many ramparts, you plotted for the royal house, set the age right, repaid the lord, settled the state and sheltered the people?

sentences.zh: 此所以五尺童子，皆願荷戟而隨將軍者也。

translations.literal: This is why boys five feet tall all wished to carry halberds and follow the general.
translations.idiomatic: This is why boys five feet tall all wished to carry halberds and follow you.

sentences.zh: 及高祖武皇肇基草昧，初濟艱難。

translations.literal: When the Founder Martial Emperor first laid foundation in the grass and darkness and first crossed hardship.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder Martial Emperor first laid foundation in grass and darkness and first crossed hardship,

sentences.zh: [8]于時天下沸騰，民無定主，豺狼當道，鯨鯢橫擊，海內業業，未知所從。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 8. At that time the realm boiled, the people had no fixed lord, wolves and jackals blocked the road, whales and krakens struck across, within the seas all were fearful and did not know whom to follow.
translations.idiomatic: [8] the realm boiled, the people had no fixed lord, wolves blocked the road, whales struck across, within the seas all were fearful and did not know whom to follow.

sentences.zh: 將軍運動微之鑒，折從衡之辯，策名委質，自託宗盟，此將軍妙筭遠圖，發於衷誠者也。

translations.literal: The general moved with the discernment of minute signs, broke the persuasions of vertical and horizontal alliance, registered his name and entrusted his person, trusting himself to the clan alliance—this is the general's subtle reckoning and far design, issuing from sincere heart.
translations.idiomatic: You moved with discernment of minute signs, broke vertical-and-horizontal persuasions, registered your name and entrusted your person to the clan alliance—this is subtle reckoning and far design from a sincere heart.

sentences.zh: 及主上繼業，欽明睿聖，選賢與能，群臣輯睦，結將軍以維城之重，崇將軍以裂土之封。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven succeeded the enterprise, he was reverent, bright, and sage, chose the worthy and employed the able, ministers were harmonious; he bound the general with the weight of a wall city and honored the general with enfeoffment splitting the soil.
translations.idiomatic: When the Son of Heaven succeeded, reverent, bright, and sage, he chose the worthy and employed the able, ministers were harmonious; he bound you with a wall city's weight and honored you with enfeoffment splitting the soil.

sentences.zh: 豈非宏謨廟略，推赤心於物也？

translations.literal: Is it not great design of the temple altars, pushing the red heart upon things?
translations.idiomatic: Is it not great temple design, pushing the red heart upon things?

sentences.zh: 屢申明詔，款篤殷勤，君臣之分定矣，骨肉之恩深矣。

translations.literal: Again and again he made clear edicts, sincere and earnest in kindness; lord and minister's division was settled, flesh-and-blood affection was deep.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again he made clear edicts, sincere and earnest; lord and minister's division was settled, flesh-and-blood affection deep.

sentences.zh: 不意將軍惑於邪說，遽生異計，寄所以疾首痛心，泣盡繼之以血。

translations.literal: I did not expect the general, deluded by evil persuasion, suddenly to harbor a different plan—therefore Ji grieves with head in pain, weeping until blood follows the tears.
translations.idiomatic: I did not expect you, deluded by evil persuasion, suddenly to harbor a different plan—therefore I grieve with head in pain, weeping until blood follows tears.

sentences.zh: [9]萬全之策，竊為將軍惜之。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 9. The plan of ten thousand completeness—your servant privately grieves for the general.
translations.idiomatic: [9] The plan of ten thousand completeness—your servant privately grieves for you.

sentences.zh: 寄雖疾侵耄及，言無足採，千慮一得，請陳愚筭。

translations.literal: Though Ji's illness invades old age and his words are not worth gathering, in a thousand thoughts one may gain—please let me state my foolish reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Though my illness invades old age and my words are not worth gathering, in a thousand thoughts one may gain—please let me state my foolish reckoning.

sentences.zh: 願將軍少戢雷霆，賒其晷刻，使得盡狂瞽之說，披肝膽之誠，則雖死之日，由生之年也。

translations.literal: I wish the general would slightly curb thunder, grant a moment's delay, so that I may fully speak my reckless blindness and lay bare liver and gall's sincerity—then though the day of death would be the year of life.
translations.idiomatic: I wish you would slightly curb thunder, grant a moment's delay, so I may fully speak my reckless blindness and lay bare liver and gall—then though the day of death would be the year of life.

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 10.
translations.idiomatic: See editorial note 10.

sentences.zh: 自天厭梁德，多難荐臻，寰宇分崩，英雄互起，不可勝紀，人人自以為得之。

translations.literal: From Heaven's loathing of Liang's virtue, many hardships piled up, the realm split apart, heroes rose one after another beyond counting—each man thought he had gained it.
translations.idiomatic: From Heaven's loathing of Liang's virtue, hardships piled up, the realm split apart, heroes rose beyond counting—each thought he had gained it.

sentences.zh: 然夷凶翦亂，拯溺扶危，四海樂推，三靈眷命，揖讓而居南面者，陳氏也。

translations.literal: Yet to level the barbarian and cut chaos, save the drowning and support the tottering, the four seas gladly pushed forward, the three numina favored the mandate—the one who yielded and sat facing south was the house of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to level the barbarian and cut chaos, save the drowning and support the tottering, the four seas pushed forward, the three numina favored the mandate—who yielded and sat facing south was the house of Chen.

sentences.zh: 豈非歷數有在，惟天所授，當璧應運？

translations.literal: Is it not that the sequence was fixed, Heaven alone bestowed it, the jade disk answered the fortune?
translations.idiomatic: Is it not that the sequence was fixed, Heaven alone bestowed it, the jade disk answered fortune?

sentences.zh: 其事甚明，一也。

translations.literal: The matter is very clear—first point.
translations.idiomatic: The matter is very clear—first point.

sentences.zh: 主上

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven

translations.literal: (enter)
translations.idiomatic: (enter)

sentences.zh: 〔承〕基，[11]明德遠被，天綱再張，地維重紐。

translations.literal: [succeed] the foundation, Editorial footnote marker 11. bright virtue spread far, Heaven's net spread again, Earth's cord was newly tied.
translations.idiomatic: [succeed] the foundation, [11] bright virtue spread far, Heaven's net spread again, Earth's cord was newly tied.

sentences.zh: 夫以王琳之彊，侯瑱之力，進足以搖蕩中原，爭衡天下，退足以屈強江外，雄張偏隅。

translations.literal: As for Wang Lin's strength and Hou Zhen's force—advancing they were enough to shake the central plains and contend for the realm; retreating enough to bend the strong beyond the Yangzi and spread might in a corner.
translations.idiomatic: As for Wang Lin's strength and Hou Zhen's force—advancing enough to shake the central plains and contend for the realm; retreating enough to bend the strong beyond the Yangzi and spread might in a corner.

sentences.zh: 然或命一旅之師，或資一士之說，琳則瓦解冰泮，投身異域，瑱則厥角稽顙，委命闕廷。

translations.literal: Yet whether ordering a single column of troops or relying on a single scholar's persuasion, Lin then dissolved like ice, threw himself into a foreign land; Zhen then touched horn and bowed forehead, entrusted his fate at the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whether ordering a single column or relying on one scholar's persuasion, Lin dissolved like ice and threw himself into a foreign land; Zhen touched horn, bowed forehead, and entrusted fate at the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 斯又天假之威，而除其患。

translations.literal: This again is Heaven lending its prestige and removing their trouble.
translations.idiomatic: This again is Heaven lending prestige and removing their trouble.

sentences.zh: 其事甚明，二也。

translations.literal: The matter is very clear—second point.
translations.idiomatic: The matter is very clear—second point.

sentences.zh: 今將軍以藩戚之重，東南之眾，盡忠奉上，戮力勤王，豈不勳高竇融，寵過吳芮，析珪判野，南面稱孤？

translations.literal: Now the general, with the weight of a frontier kinsman and the masses of the southeast, exhausts loyalty in serving above and joins strength in diligent service to the king—is not merit higher than Dou Rong's, favor passing Wu Rui's, splitting jade tallies and judging fields, facing south and calling himself solitary?
translations.idiomatic: Now you, with a frontier kinsman's weight and the southeast's masses, exhaust loyalty serving above and join strength in diligent service to the king—is not merit higher than Dou Rong's, favor passing Wu Rui's, splitting jade tallies and judging fields, facing south and calling yourself solitary?

sentences.zh: 其事甚明，三也。

translations.literal: The matter is very clear—third point.
translations.idiomatic: The matter is very clear—third point.

sentences.zh: 且聖朝棄瑕忘過，寬厚得人，改過自新，咸加敘擢。

translations.literal: Moreover the holy court discards flaws and forgets faults, is broad and thick in gaining men; those who reform and renew themselves are all promoted in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the holy court discards flaws and forgets faults, is broad in gaining men; those who reform are all promoted in turn.

sentences.zh: 至於余孝頃、潘純陀、李孝欽、歐陽頠等，悉委以心腹，任以爪牙，胸中豁然，曾無纖芥。

translations.literal: As for Yu Xiaoxu, Pan Chuntuo, Li Xiaoqin, Ouyang Yi, and the rest—all were entrusted with inmost heart, employed as talon and tooth; the breast was open and never had the slightest mote.
translations.idiomatic: As for Yu Xiaoxu, Pan Chuntuo, Li Xiaoqin, Ouyang Yi, and the rest—all were entrusted with inmost heart, employed as talon and tooth; the breast was open without the slightest mote.

sentences.zh: 況將軍舋非張繡，罪異畢諶，當何慮於危亡，何失於富貴？

translations.literal: How much more is the general's rising not Zhang Xiu's, his crime unlike Bi Chen's—what worry of peril and extinction, what loss of wealth and honor?
translations.idiomatic: How much more—your rising is not Zhang Xiu's, your crime unlike Bi Chen's—what worry of peril, what loss of wealth and honor?

sentences.zh: 此又其事甚明，四也。

translations.literal: This again—the matter is very clear, fourth point.
translations.idiomatic: This again—the matter is very clear, fourth point.

sentences.zh: 方今周、齊鄰睦，境外無虞，并兵一向，匪朝伊夕，非劉、項競逐之機，楚、趙連從之勢，何得雍容高拱，坐論西伯？

translations.literal: Now Zhou and Qi are neighbors in harmony, beyond the borders without worry; joining troops in one direction is not morning or evening away—it is not the moment of Liu and Xiang contending, nor the momentum of Chu and Zhao joining—how may one sit at ease with high hands folded and sit discussing the Western Earl?
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhou and Qi are neighbors in harmony, beyond the borders without worry; joining troops in one direction is not morning or evening away—not Liu and Xiang contending, nor Chu and Zhao joining—how may one sit at ease with hands folded and discuss the Western Earl?

sentences.zh: 其事甚明，五也。

translations.literal: The matter is very clear—fifth point.
translations.idiomatic: The matter is very clear—fifth point.

sentences.zh: 且留將軍狼顧一隅，亟經摧衄，聲實虧喪，膽氣衰沮。

translations.literal: Moreover General Liu glares wolf-like in a corner, repeatedly beaten and broken, fame and substance wasted, courage and spirit decayed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover General Liu glares wolf-like in a corner, repeatedly beaten, fame and substance wasted, courage decayed.

sentences.zh: 高瓖、向文政、留瑜、黃子玉，此數人者，將軍所知，首鼠兩端，唯利是視；

translations.literal: Gao Zan, Xiang Wenzheng, Liu Yu, Huang Ziyu—these several men, the general knows them: rats with two heads, seeing only profit;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zan, Xiang Wenzheng, Liu Yu, Huang Ziyu—these several, you know them: rats with two heads, seeing only profit;

sentences.zh: 其餘將帥，亦可見矣。

translations.literal: as for the rest of the generals, they may also be seen.
translations.idiomatic: as for the rest of the generals, they may also be seen.

sentences.zh: 孰能被堅執銳，長驅深入，繫馬埋輪，奮不顧命，以先士卒者乎？

translations.literal: Who can don hard armor and grasp sharp edge, drive deep in long march, tie horses and bury wheels, strive without regard for life, and go before the soldiers?
translations.idiomatic: Who can don hard armor and grasp sharp edge, drive deep in long march, tie horses and bury wheels, strive without regard for life, and go before the soldiers?

sentences.zh: 此又其事甚明，六也。

translations.literal: This again—the matter is very clear, sixth point.
translations.idiomatic: This again—the matter is very clear, sixth point.

sentences.zh: 且將軍之彊，孰如侯景？

translations.literal: Moreover is the general's strength like Hou Jing's?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover is your strength like Hou Jing's?

sentences.zh: 將軍之眾，孰如王琳？

translations.literal: Are the general's masses like Wang Lin's?
translations.idiomatic: Are your masses like Wang Lin's?

sentences.zh: 武皇滅侯景於前，今上摧王琳於後，此乃天時，非復人力。

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor destroyed Hou Jing before; the present sovereign broke Wang Lin after—this is Heaven's season, no longer human power.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder destroyed Hou Jing before; the present sovereign broke Wang Lin after—this is Heaven's season, no longer human power.

sentences.zh: 且兵革已後，民皆厭亂，其孰能棄墳墓，捐妻子，出萬死不顧之計，從將軍於白刃之閒乎？

translations.literal: Moreover after arms and armor, the people all loathe disorder—who can abandon graves, cast off wife and children, go forth on a plan of ten thousand deaths without regard, and follow the general between white blades?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover after arms and armor the people loathe disorder—who can abandon graves, cast off wife and children, go forth on ten thousand deaths without regard, and follow you between white blades?

sentences.zh: 此又其事甚明，七也。

translations.literal: This again—the matter is very clear, seventh point.
translations.idiomatic: This again—the matter is very clear, seventh point.

sentences.zh: 歷觀前古，鑒之往事，子陽、季孟，傾覆相尋，餘善、

translations.literal: Looking through former antiquity and taking mirror from past affairs, Ziyang, Jimeng, overturn followed in succession; Yu Shan and
translations.idiomatic: Looking through antiquity and taking mirror from past affairs, Ziyang, Jimeng, overturn followed in succession; Yu Shan and

translations.literal: (stone)
translations.idiomatic: (stone)

sentences.zh: 〔右〕渠，[12]危亡繼及，天命可畏，山川難恃。

translations.literal: [Right] Canal, Editorial footnote marker 12. peril and extinction followed in turn—Heaven's mandate may be feared, mountains and rivers are hard to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: [Right] Canal, [12] peril and extinction followed in turn—Heaven's mandate may be feared, mountains and rivers are hard to rely on.

sentences.zh: 況將軍欲以數郡之地，當天下之兵，以諸侯之資，拒天子之命，彊弱逆順，可得侔乎？

translations.literal: How much more when the general wishes with the territory of several commanderies to meet the realm's troops, with a feudal lord's resources to resist the Son of Heaven's command—strong and weak, obedience and rebellion, can they be matched?
translations.idiomatic: How much more when you wish with several commanderies' territory to meet the realm's troops, with a feudal lord's resources to resist the Son of Heaven's command—strong and weak, obedience and rebellion, can they be matched?

sentences.zh: 此又其事甚明，八也。

translations.literal: This again—the matter is very clear, eighth point.
translations.idiomatic: This again—the matter is very clear, eighth point.

sentences.zh: 且非我族類，其心必異。

translations.literal: Moreover those not of our kindred—their hearts must differ.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover those not of our kindred—their hearts must differ.

sentences.zh: 不愛其親，豈能及物？

translations.literal: If one does not love his kin, how can he reach to things?
translations.idiomatic: If one does not love his kin, how can he reach to things?

sentences.zh: 留將軍身縻國爵，子尚王姬，猶且棄天屬而弗顧，背明君而孤立，危急之日，豈能同憂共患，不背將軍者乎？

translations.literal: General Liu himself is bound by the state's rank, his son is still married to a king's daughter—yet he still abandons Heaven's kin and does not look back, turns his back on the bright lord and stands alone—in days of peril and urgency, how can they share worry and disaster and not turn their backs on the general?
translations.idiomatic: General Liu is bound by the state's rank, his son married to a king's daughter—yet he abandons Heaven's kin, turns his back on the bright lord and stands alone—in days of peril, how can they share worry and not turn their backs on you?

sentences.zh: 至於師老力屈，懼誅利賞，必有韓、智晉陽之謀，張、陳井陘之勢。

translations.literal: As for the army old and strength spent, fearing punishment and coveting reward, there must be the schemes of Han and Zhi at Jinyang, the momentum of Zhang and Chen at Jingxing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When the army is old and strength spent, fearing punishment and coveting reward, there must be Han and Zhi's schemes at Jinyang, Zhang and Chen's momentum at Jingxing Pass.

sentences.zh: 此又其事甚明，九也。

translations.literal: This again—the matter is very clear, ninth point.
translations.idiomatic: This again—the matter is very clear, ninth point.

sentences.zh: 且北軍萬里遠鬥，鋒不可當，將軍自戰其地，人多顧後。

translations.literal: Moreover the northern army fights a myriad li away; its edge cannot be withstood—the general fights on his own ground and many men look behind.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the northern army fights a myriad li away; its edge cannot be withstood—you fight on your own ground and many look behind.

sentences.zh: 梁安背向為心，修旿匹夫之力，眾寡不敵，將帥不侔，師以無名而出，事以無機而動，以此稱兵，未知其利。

translations.literal: Liang An's heart turns away, Xiu Xu's strength is a single man—the many cannot match the few, generals cannot compare with commanders; the army goes forth without a name, the affair moves without opportunity—raising troops thus, one does not know its profit.
translations.idiomatic: Liang An's heart turns away, Xiu Xu's strength is a single man—the many cannot match the few, generals cannot compare; the army goes forth without a name, the affair moves without opportunity—raising troops thus, one does not know its profit.

sentences.zh: 夫以漢朝吳、楚，晉室穎、顒，連城數十，長戟百萬，拔本塞源，自圖家國，其有成功者乎？

translations.literal: As for Han's Wu and Chu, Jin's Ying and Yong—linked cities by the tens, long halberds by the million, uprooting the root and blocking the source to plot their own house and state—were there any who succeeded?
translations.idiomatic: As for Han's Wu and Chu, Jin's Ying and Yong—linked cities by the tens, long halberds by the million, uprooting root and blocking source to plot house and state—were there any who succeeded?

sentences.zh: 此又其事甚明，十也。

translations.literal: This again—the matter is very clear, tenth point.
translations.idiomatic: This again—the matter is very clear, tenth point.

sentences.zh: 為將軍計者，莫若不遠而復，絕親留氏，秦郎、快郎，隨遣入質，釋甲偃兵，一遵詔旨。

translations.literal: For the general's reckoning, there is none better than not going far and returning, breaking kinship with the Liu clan, sending Qin Lang and Kuai Lang promptly as hostages, laying down armor and stilling troops, wholly following the edict.
translations.idiomatic: For your reckoning, none better than not going far and returning, breaking kinship with the Liu clan, sending Qin Lang and Kuai Lang promptly as hostages, laying down armor and stilling troops, wholly following the edict.

sentences.zh: 且朝廷許以鐵券之要，申以白馬之盟，朕弗食言，誓之宗社。

translations.literal: Moreover the court promises the covenant of the iron certificate and declares the white-horse alliance—I will not eat my words and swear it to the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the court promises the iron certificate covenant and declares the white-horse alliance—I will not eat my words and swear it to the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 寄聞明者鑒未形，智者不再計，此成敗之效，將軍勿疑。

translations.literal: Ji has heard that the clear-sighted mirror what is not yet formed, the wise do not reckon twice—this is the effect of success and failure; the general must not doubt.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the clear-sighted mirror what is not yet formed, the wise do not reckon twice—this is the effect of success and failure; you must not doubt.

sentences.zh: 吉凶之幾，間不容髮。

translations.literal: The fine line of fortune and calamity admits no hair's breadth between.
translations.idiomatic: The fine line of fortune and calamity admits no hair's breadth between.

sentences.zh: 方今藩維尚少，皇子幼沖，凡預宗枝，皆蒙寵樹。

translations.literal: Now frontier screens are still few, the princes young and tender; all who share the clan branch are showered with favor and planting.
translations.idiomatic: Now frontier screens are still few, princes young and tender; all who share the clan branch are showered with favor.

sentences.zh: 況以將軍之地，將軍之才，將軍之名，將軍之勢，而能克修藩服，北面稱臣，寧與劉澤同年而語其功業哉？

translations.literal: How much more with the general's territory, the general's talent, the general's name, and the general's power—yet able to cultivate the fief in full, face north and call himself subject: could he speak of his achievements in the same year as Liu Ze?
translations.idiomatic: With your territory, talent, name, and power, if you could truly keep your fief in order and face north as a subject, could your achievement be named in the same breath as Liu Ze's?

sentences.zh: 豈不身與山河等安，名與金石相敝？

translations.literal: Would not body and rivers-and-mountains share equal peace, and name and metal-and-stone wear out together?
translations.idiomatic: Would not your person share the peace of the realm and your name endure like bronze and stone?

sentences.zh: 願加三思，慮之無忽。

translations.literal: I wish you would add thrice-over thought and consider it without neglect.
translations.idiomatic: Please think it over again and again and do not overlook it.

sentences.zh: 寄氣力綿微，餘陰無幾，感恩懷德，不覺狂言，鈇鉞之誅，甘之如薺。

translations.literal: Ji—his vital force is thin and slight, his remaining shade has little left; grateful for grace and cherishing virtue, he does not notice his wild words; execution by axe and yue, he would find sweet as shepherd's purse.
translations.idiomatic: My strength is failing and little time remains; grateful for your kindness, I speak rashly without thinking. If the axe falls on me, I shall take it as gladly as shepherd's purse.

sentences.zh: 寶應覽書大怒。

translations.literal: Baoying, reading the letter, was greatly angry.
translations.idiomatic: Baoying read the letter and flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 或謂寶應曰：「虞公病勢漸篤，言多錯謬。

translations.literal: Someone said to Baoying: "Lord Yu's illness grows daily worse; his words are mostly mistaken and absurd.
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Baoying, "Lord Yu's illness is worsening; his words are mostly confused.

sentences.zh: 」寶應意乃小釋。

translations.literal: " Baoying's mind then eased somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: " Baoying's anger eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 亦為寄有民望，且優容之。

translations.literal: Also because Ji had the people's regard, he moreover treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Also because Ji enjoyed public esteem, he treated him with forbearance.

sentences.zh: 及寶應敗走，夜至蒲田，顧謂其子扞秦曰：「早從虞公計，不至今日。

translations.literal: When Baoying was defeated and fled, at night he reached Putian, turned and said to his son Han Qin: "Had we early followed Lord Yu's plan, we would not have come to today.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoying was defeated and fled, he reached Putian by night and said to his son Han Qin, "Had we followed Lord Yu's counsel sooner, we would not be here today.

sentences.zh: 」扞秦但泣而已。

translations.literal: " Han Qin only wept, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: " Han Qin could only weep.

sentences.zh: 寶應既擒，凡諸賓客微有交涉者，皆伏誅，唯寄以先識免禍。

translations.literal: When Baoying was captured, of all the guests who had the slightest connection, all were put to death; only Ji, because of prior acquaintance, escaped calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoying was taken, every guest who had had dealings with him was executed; only Ji, through prior acquaintance, escaped.

sentences.zh: 初，沙門慧摽涉獵有才思，及寶應起兵，作五言詩以送之，曰：「送馬猶臨水，離旗稍引風，好看今夜月，當入紫微宮。

translations.literal: Initially the monk Huibiao ranged widely and had talent and thought; when Baoying raised troops, he composed a five-character poem to send him off, saying: "Sending horses still by the water, parting banners slightly catch the wind; behold tonight's moon—it should enter the Purple Forbidden Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the monk Huibiao was widely read and clever. When Baoying took up arms, Huibiao sent him a five-character poem: "Horses still water the parting stream; banners catch the wind; see how tonight's moon should enter the Purple Forbidden Palace.

sentences.zh: 」寶應得之甚悅。

translations.literal: " Baoying, obtaining it, was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " Baoying was delighted with it.

sentences.zh: 慧摽賷以示寄，寄一覽便止，正色無言。

translations.literal: Huibiao brought it to show Ji; Ji read it once and stopped, with stern countenance and no words.
translations.idiomatic: Huibiao showed it to Ji. Ji read it once, set it down, and said nothing, his face stern.

sentences.zh: 摽退，寄謂所親曰：「摽公既以此始，必以此終。

translations.literal: Huibiao withdrew; Ji said to those close to him: "Master Biao began with this—he will end with this.
translations.idiomatic: When Huibiao left, Ji told his intimates, "Master Biao began with this; he will end with this.

sentences.zh: 」後竟坐是誅。

translations.literal: " Later he was indeed executed on this account.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he was executed for it.

sentences.zh: 文帝尋敕都督章昭達以理發遣，令寄還朝。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen soon ordered Area Commander Zhang Zhaoda to arrange his dismissal and send Ji back to court.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen soon ordered Area Commander Zhang Zhaoda to send Ji home to court.

sentences.zh: 及至，即日引見，謂寄曰：「管寧無恙。

translations.literal: When he arrived, that very day he was granted audience; he said to Ji: "Guan Ning is unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he was received that same day. The emperor said to Ji, "Guan Ning is well.

sentences.zh: 」其慰勞之懷若此。

translations.literal: His mind to comfort and reward was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his warmth in greeting him.

sentences.zh: 頃之，文帝謂到仲舉曰：「 衡陽王既出閤，雖未置府僚，然須得一人旦夕遊處，兼掌書記，宜求宿士有行業者。

translations.literal: Before long Emperor Wen said to Dao Zhongju: "The Prince of Hengyang has left the inner quarters; though he has not yet been given palace staff, yet there must be one man to pass the day with him morning and evening and also keep the records—I should seek an elder scholar of established conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Emperor Wen told Dao Zhongju, "Prince Hengyang has left the inner palace. Though he has no staff yet, he needs someone with him day and night who can also keep his records. We should find a senior man of real conduct.

sentences.zh: 」仲舉未知所對，文帝曰：「吾自得之。

translations.literal: " Zhongju did not know how to answer; the emperor said: "I have already found him.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongju had no answer. The emperor said, "I already have the man.

sentences.zh: 」乃手敕用寄。

translations.literal: " Thereupon by hand-edict he employed Ji.
translations.idiomatic: " He then appointed Ji by personal edict.

sentences.zh: 寄入謝，文帝曰：「所以蹔屈卿遊藩者，非止以文翰相煩，乃令以師表相事也。

translations.literal: Ji entered to give thanks; the emperor said: "The reason I temporarily bend you to roam the fief is not only to trouble you with documents—it is also to have you serve him as teacher and model.
translations.idiomatic: Ji came to give thanks. The emperor said, "I bend you to the prince's household not only for paperwork but to be his teacher and example.

sentences.zh: 」尋兼散騎常侍，聘齊，寄辭老疾，不行，除國子博士。

translations.literal: " Soon he was concurrently made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; as envoy to Qi, Ji declined on grounds of age and illness and did not go; he was made Doctor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: " He was soon made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and sent as envoy to Qi, but Ji pleaded age and illness and did not go; he was made doctor of the national university.

sentences.zh: 頃之，又表求解職歸鄉里，文帝優旨報答，許其東還。

translations.literal: Before long he also memorialized requesting to leave office and return to his home village; the emperor answered with a gracious edict and permitted him to go east.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he memorialized to resign and return home; the emperor answered graciously and let him go east.

sentences.zh: 仍除東揚州別駕，寄又以疾辭。

translations.literal: He was then made Vice-Prefect of East Yangzhou; Ji again declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made vice-prefect of East Yangzhou; Ji again pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，徵授揚州治中及尚書左丞，並不就。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao Zong succeeded, he was summoned and appointed Yangzhou Administrator-in-Chief and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, but he did not accept either post.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao Zong succeeded, he was summoned as Yangzhou administrator-in-chief and left vice director of the masters of writing, but accepted neither.

sentences.zh: 乃除東中郎建安王諮議，加戎昭將軍，又辭以疾，不任旦夕陪列。

translations.literal: He was then made Adviser to the Eastern Palace General of the Prince of Jian'an, with the added title General Who Displays Martial Prestige; again he declined on grounds of illness, unable to attend morning and evening in the train.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made adviser to the prince of Jian'an, eastern palace general, with the added title general who displays martial prestige, but again pleaded illness and could not attend daily.

sentences.zh: 王於是特令停王府公事，其有疑議，就以決之，但朔望牋修而已。

translations.literal: The prince therefore specially ordered a halt to princely-house business; when there were doubtful points, Ji was consulted to decide them—only on the first and fifteenth of the month did he draft the routine memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The prince then stopped routine palace business for him; doubtful matters were referred to Ji for decision; he only drafted the regular memorial on the first and fifteenth of the month.

sentences.zh: 太建八年加太中大夫，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taijian he was advanced to Grand Master of Palace Counsel; his general's title was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 8 he was advanced to grand master of palace counsel, retaining his general's title.

sentences.zh: 十一年卒，時年七十。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 he died, aged seventy.

sentences.zh: 寄少篤行，造次必於仁厚，雖僮豎未嘗加以聲色，至於臨危執節，則辭氣凜然，白刃不憚也。

translations.literal: From youth Ji was devoted in conduct; even in haste he was always generous and mild; though servants and boys he never addressed with harsh voice or color; yet when facing peril and holding to integrity, then his words and spirit were stern and cold, and he did not fear bare blades.
