translations.idiomatic: From youth Ji was steadfast in conduct; even in haste he was gentle and never raised his voice at servants or boys; yet in danger he held firm, his words icy, and he did not flinch from naked blades.

sentences.zh: 自流寓南土，與兄荔隔絕，因感氣病，每得荔書，氣輒奔劇，危殆者數矣。

translations.literal: From the time he was cast adrift in the southern lands, separated from his elder brother Li by a barrier, he therefore suffered from qi illness; whenever he received a letter from Li, his qi would rush into violent fits, and several times he was at the brink of death.
translations.idiomatic: After he was stranded in the south, cut off from his brother Li, he suffered from a breathing disorder; each letter from Li brought on violent fits and several times nearly killed him.

sentences.zh: 前後所居官，未嘗至秩滿，纔期年數月，便自求解退。

translations.literal: In every office he held, he never reached the full term; only a year or several months, and he would himself request to resign and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he never served a full term; after a year or a few months he would ask to resign.

sentences.zh: 常曰：「知足不辱，吾知足矣。

translations.literal: He often said: "Knowing sufficiency brings no disgrace—I know sufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "Knowing when one has enough avoids disgrace—and I have enough.

sentences.zh: 」及謝病私庭，每諸王為州將，下車必造門致禮，命釋鞭板，以几杖侍坐。

translations.literal: " When he took leave for illness in his private home, whenever a prince was made area commander, on descending from his carriage he would always come to the gate with ritual; Ji was ordered to set aside whip and tablet and sit with a armrest and staff.
translations.idiomatic: " In retirement at home, whenever a prince became area commander and alighted from his carriage, he came to Ji's gate with full ceremony; Ji was told to lay aside whip and writing board and receive him seated with staff and armrest.

sentences.zh: 常出遊近寺，閭里傳相告語，老幼羅列，望拜道左。

translations.literal: When he often went out to visit nearby temples, the lanes and hamlets would pass word to one another; old and young lined the roads, looking up and bowing on the left of the way.
translations.idiomatic: When he went to nearby temples, neighbors spread word; old and young lined the road and bowed as he passed.

sentences.zh: 或言誓為約者，但指寄便不欺，其至行所感如此。

translations.literal: Some who swore oaths as pledges would only point to Ji and not deceive—such was the reach of his supreme conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Men who swore oaths would point to Ji and keep their word—such was the force of his conduct.

sentences.zh: 所製文筆，遭亂多不存。

translations.literal: The writings he composed, in the disorders were mostly not preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Most of what he wrote was lost in the disorders.

sentences.zh: 馬樞字要理，扶風郿人也。

translations.literal: Ma Shu, styled Yaoli, was a native of Mei in Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shu, styled Yaoli, was from Mei in Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 祖靈慶，齊竟陵王錄事參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lingqing was a Recorder in the Prince of Jingling's household under Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lingqing had been recorder in the household of the prince of Jingling under Qi.

sentences.zh: 樞數歲而父母俱喪，為其姑所養。

translations.literal: When Shu was several years old both parents died; he was reared by his paternal aunt.
translations.idiomatic: Shu lost both parents as a small child and was raised by his father's sister.

sentences.zh: 六歲，能誦孝經、論語、老子。

translations.literal: At age six he could recite the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, and the Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: At six he could recite the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, and the Laozi.

sentences.zh: 及長，博極經史，尤善佛經及周易、老子義。

translations.literal: When grown, he ranged to the limit through the classics and histories, and was especially skilled in Buddhist sutras and the meaning of the Changes and the Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: Grown up, he was deeply read in the classics and histories and especially skilled in Buddhist sutras and the exegesis of the Changes and Laozi.

sentences.zh: 梁邵陵王綸為南徐州刺史，素聞其名，引為學士。

translations.literal: Liang's Prince of Shaoling Xiao Lun was Inspector of South Xuzhou; having long heard his name, he summoned him as academician.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Lun, prince of Shaoling, was inspector of South Xuzhou; he had long heard of Shu and made him an academician.

sentences.zh: 綸時自講大品經，令樞講維摩、老子、周易，同日發題，道俗聽者二千人。

translations.literal: Lun at the time himself lectured on the Great Perfection Sutra and had Shu lecture on the Vimalakirti, the Laozi, and the Changes, setting topics the same day; clergy and laity who listened numbered two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Lun then lectured on the Great Perfection Sutra himself and had Shu lecture on the Vimalakirti, Laozi, and Changes the same day; two thousand clergy and laymen listened.

sentences.zh: 王欲極觀優劣，乃謂眾曰：「與馬學士論義，必使屈伏，不得空立主客。

translations.literal: The prince wished to observe fully the superior and inferior; he therefore said to the assembly: "In disputation with Academician Ma, you must make him yield—do not stand empty as guest and host.
translations.idiomatic: The prince wished to test who was stronger and told the crowd, "In debate with Academician Ma you must make him yield; do not leave guest and host empty.

sentences.zh: 」於是數家學者各起問端，樞乃依次剖判，開其宗旨，然後枝分流別，轉變無窮，論者拱默聽受而已。

translations.literal: " Thereupon several families of scholars each rose to pose questions; Shu then in sequence analyzed and judged, opening their main points, then branching into streams and divisions, turning and changing without end; the debaters bowed in silence and only listened—Lun greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: " Several schools of scholars each raised questions. Shu answered in turn, opened each main point, then branched into endless distinctions; the debaters bowed and listened in silence. Lun was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 綸甚嘉之，將引薦於朝廷。

translations.literal: Lun wished to recommend him to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Lun meant to recommend him at court.

sentences.zh: 尋遇侯景之亂，綸舉兵援臺，乃留書二萬卷以付樞。

translations.literal: Soon he encountered Hou Jing's rebellion; Lun raised troops to aid the Terrace City and left twenty thousand scrolls of books entrusted to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon came Hou Jing's rebellion. Lun raised troops to aid the capital and left twenty thousand scrolls with Shu.

sentences.zh: 樞肆志尋覽，殆將周遍，乃喟然歎曰：「吾聞貴爵位者以巢、由為桎梏，愛山林者以伊、呂為管庫，束名實則芻芥柱下之言，翫清虛則糠秕席上之說，稽之篤論，亦各從其好也。

translations.literal: Shu with full intent searched and read them, nearly covering all; he then sighed and said: "I have heard that those who prize rank and title take Chao and Jufu as fetters, and those who love mountains and forests take Yi and Lü as granary keepers; binding name and reality makes Zhuangzi's words mere hay; playing with emptiness and purity makes seat-side doctrines mere chaff; checked against earnest discourse, each also follows his own preference.
translations.idiomatic: Shu read through them almost entirely and sighed: "I hear that men who prize office take Chao and Jufu as shackles, and men who love the hills take Yi and Lü as storekeepers; those who bind name to fact treat Zhuangzi as straw, and those who play at emptiness treat banquet talk as chaff. In earnest judgment each follows his own bent.

sentences.zh: 然支父有讓王之介，嚴子有傲帝之規，千載美談，所不廢也。

translations.literal: Yet Zhi Fu had the manner of yielding the kingship, and Yan Zi had the plan of defying the emperor—thousand-year fine tales that are not abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhi Fu refused the throne, and Yan Zi defied his ruler—tales a thousand years old that are not forgotten.

sentences.zh: 比求志之士，望塗而息。

translations.literal: Compared with seekers of resolve today, they gaze at the road and cease.
translations.idiomatic: Beside men who seek resolve today, they stop at the roadside and turn back.

sentences.zh: 豈天之不惠高尚，何山林之無聞甚乎？

translations.literal: Is it that Heaven does not favor the lofty, or why are the hills and forests so little heard of?
translations.idiomatic: Does Heaven not favor the high-minded, or why are recluses so seldom heard of?

sentences.zh: 」乃隱于茅山，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: " He then hid on Mount Mao, with the will to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: " He then retired to Mount Mao, intending to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，文帝徵為度支尚書，辭不應命。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjia, Emperor Wen summoned him as Director of Revenue; he declined and did not answer the command.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 1 Emperor Wen summoned him as director of revenue; he declined and did not answer.

sentences.zh: 時樞親故並居京口，每秋冬之際，時往遊焉。

translations.literal: At that time Shu's kin and old friends all dwelt at Jingkou; each year at the turn of autumn and winter he would go to visit them.
translations.idiomatic: His kin and friends then lived at Jingkou; each autumn and winter he visited them.

sentences.zh: 及鄱陽王為南徐州刺史，欽其高尚，鄙不能致，乃卑辭厚意，令使者邀之，前後數反，樞固辭以疾。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Poyang was Inspector of South Xuzhou, admiring his loftiness and despising his inability to summon him, he therefore used humble words and thick kindness, ordering envoys to invite him—several times back and forth—yet Shu firmly declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince of Poyang was inspector of South Xuzhou, he admired Shu's loftiness but could not summon him; he used humble words and rich courtesy and sent envoys again and again, but Shu firmly pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 門人或進曰：「鄱陽王待以師友，非關爵位，市朝之間，何妨靜默。

translations.literal: A disciple advanced and said: "The Prince of Poyang treats you as teacher and friend—it is not about rank; amid market and court, what harm in keeping silence?
translations.idiomatic: A disciple urged him, "The prince of Poyang treats you as teacher and friend, not for rank. What harm in quiet presence amid court and market?

sentences.zh: 」樞不得已，乃行。

translations.literal: " Shu, having no way out, then went.
translations.idiomatic: " Shu, unable to refuse further, went.

sentences.zh: 王別築室以處之，樞惡其崇麗，乃於竹林間自營茅茨而居焉。

translations.literal: The prince separately built a chamber to house him; Shu hated its grandeur and splendor and therefore in the bamboo grove built his own thatched hut to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: The prince built him a separate house; Shu disliked its splendor and made a thatched hut in the bamboo grove.

sentences.zh: 每王公餽餉，辭不獲已者，率十分受一。

translations.literal: Whenever princes and dukes sent gifts, of those he could not decline, he generally accepted one part in ten.
translations.idiomatic: When princes sent gifts he could not refuse, he usually took one part in ten.

sentences.zh: 樞少屬亂離，每所居之處，盜賊不入，依託者常數百家。

translations.literal: Shu from youth belonged to times of disorder; in every place he dwelt, bandits did not enter; those who relied on him were often several hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Shu lived in disorder; wherever he stayed bandits did not enter, and hundreds of households often sheltered under him.

sentences.zh: 目精洞黃，能視闇中物。

translations.literal: His eye pupils were penetrating yellow and could see objects in the dark.
translations.idiomatic: His pupils were bright yellow and could see in the dark.

sentences.zh: 常有白鷰一雙，巢其庭樹，馴狎櫩廡，時集几案，春來秋去，幾三十年。

translations.literal: There were always a pair of white swallows that nested in the courtyard trees, tame on the eaves and verandas, sometimes perching on tables and desks; they came in spring and left in autumn—for nearly thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: A pair of white swallows always nested in his courtyard trees, tame on eaves and verandas and sometimes on his desk; spring after spring and autumn after autumn—for nearly thirty years.

sentences.zh: 太建十三年卒，時年六十。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Taijian he died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 13 he died, aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 撰道覺論二十卷行於世。

translations.literal: He composed Treatise on the Awakening of the Way in twenty scrolls, circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Treatise on the Awakening of the Way in twenty scrolls, which circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：沈炯仕於梁室，年在知命，冀郎署之薄官，[13]止邑宰之卑職，及下筆盟壇，屬辭勸表，激揚旨趣，信文人之偉者歟！

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Shen Jiong served the Liang house; in years he had reached knowing fate—he hoped for thin posts in the secretariat, [13] and stopped at the low office of district magistrate; when he set brush to the alliance altar and composed words for exhortation and memorial, rousing and lifting the aim and tone—truly a great man among men of letters!
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Shen Jiong served Liang. Past knowing fate he had hoped for a modest secretariat post [13] and rose no higher than district magistrate; yet at the alliance altar and in memorial prose his voice soared—truly a great writer.

sentences.zh: 虞荔之獻籌沈密，盡其誠款，可謂有益明時矣。

translations.literal: Yu Li's presenting stratagems was deep and close, exhausting his sincere good faith—one may say he benefited the enlightened age.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Li's counsel was deep and thorough and his loyalty complete—he truly served a bright age.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 沈炯字禮明 「禮明」南史作「初明」。

translations.literal: Shen Jiong, styled Liming—"Liming" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Chuming."
translations.idiomatic: On "Shen Jiong, styled Liming": the History of the Southern Dynasties reads Chuming.

sentences.zh: 王鳴盛《十七史商榷》引何焯說，云作「禮明」是。

translations.literal: Wang Mingsheng's Examination of Discrepancies among the Seventeen Histories cites He Zhuo's view, saying that to read "Liming" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mingsheng's Examination of Discrepancies among the Seventeen Histories cites He Zhuo: Liming is correct.

sentences.zh: 別風餘

translations.literal: Separate wind's remaining
translations.idiomatic: Separate wind's remaining

sentences.zh: 〔百〕死輕生 據南監本及《元龜》七五四改。

translations.literal: [hundred] deaths, light on life—changed according to the Southern Supervisory edition and the Comprehensive Mirror 754.
translations.idiomatic: On "[hundred] deaths, light on life": emended per the Southern Supervisory edition and Comprehensive Mirror 754.

sentences.zh: 若自虧身禮 「禮」各本並作「體」，《元龜》七五四同。

translations.literal: If he himself impaired his person in ritual—"ritual" in all editions reads "body"; the Comprehensive Mirror 754 is the same.
translations.idiomatic: On "if he himself impaired his person in ritual": all editions read body; Comprehensive Mirror 754 agrees.

sentences.zh: 按此指其自身當守之禮言，作「禮」是。

translations.literal: Comment: this refers to the ritual one should keep toward one's own person; to read "ritual" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: This refers to ritual owed one's own person; ritual is correct.

sentences.zh: 日者理切倚門 「倚門」北監本、汲本、殿本作「倚閭」。

translations.literal: Recently reason was urgent at leaning on the gate—"leaning on the gate" in the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions reads "leaning on the lane."
translations.idiomatic: On "recently reason was urgent at leaning on the gate": Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions read leaning on the lane.

sentences.zh: 按倚門、倚閭皆言望子之切，同見《戰國策·齊策》。

translations.literal: Comment: both leaning on the gate and leaning on the lane speak of a parent's keen longing for a son; both appear in the Strategies of Qi in the Intrigues of the Warring States.
translations.idiomatic: Both leaning on the gate and leaning on the lane mean a parent's longing for a son; both appear in the Qi strategies in the Intrigues of the Warring States.

translations.literal: [pare] traces in hill and garden—changed according to the Southern Supervisory, Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "[pare] traces in hill and garden": emended per the Southern Supervisory, Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.

sentences.zh: 匪獨天時 「匪」字原墨丁，據各本補。

translations.literal: It was not Heaven alone—"not" was originally an ink dot in the base text and is now supplied from the various editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "it was not Heaven alone": fei was faded in the base text and is restored from other editions.

sentences.zh: 初濟艱難 「艱」字原墨丁，據各本補。

translations.literal: At first crossing difficulty—"difficult" was originally an ink dot in the base text and is now supplied from the various editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "at first crossing difficulty": jian was faded in the base text and is restored from other editions.

sentences.zh: 泣盡繼之以血 「盡」字下北監本、汲本、殿本有「而」字。

translations.literal: Weeping exhausted, blood followed—below "exhausted" the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions have the character "and."
translations.idiomatic: On "weeping exhausted, blood followed": Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions add er after jin.

sentences.zh: 由生之年也 「由」南監本作「猶」。

translations.literal: By the years of one's birth—"by" in the Southern Supervisory reads "still."
translations.idiomatic: On "by the years of one's birth": the Southern Supervisory reads still.

sentences.zh: 按猶由通。

translations.literal: Comment: you and you are interchangeable.
translations.idiomatic: You and you are interchangeable.

sentences.zh: 按右渠西漢時朝鮮國王。

translations.literal: Comment: Right Canal was king of Korea in Western Han times.
translations.idiomatic: Right Canal was a king of Korea in Western Han.

sentences.zh: 冀郎署之薄官 「官」原訛「宦」，各本不訛，今改正。

translations.literal: Hoped for thin posts in the secretariat—"post" was originally erroneous as "office"; the various editions are not erroneous; it is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: On "hoped for thin posts in the secretariat": guan was miswritten huan in the base text; other editions read correctly; now emended.
